answer: Agents can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote, with votes weighted by stake and the lock lasting through a challenge period. Splitting one stake across a hundred accounts then adds no influence, while creating influence requires acquiring more stake and risking its forfeiture if coordinated fraud is proven. The glacier of delayed withdrawals gives honest peers time to expose a sybil cluster; a pearl of evidence can trigger review, and willow-like branching accounts still face the same capital cost.
